title: More and Fewer Word Problems
intro: Use matching rows of counters to teach more-than and fewer-than comparisons.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Build the known collection, then match it in a second row. Add or remove the difference to represent the other person's collection.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

Alex: 8 cards.

Maya: as many as Alex, plus 3 extra.

8 + 3 = 11

Maya has 11 cards. The extra 3 are only the part beyond Alex’s collection.

Ask your student

Does this number tell us the whole collection or just the difference?

If your student needs help

If the student copies the difference as the answer, have them count the entire row for the person named in the question.

Choosing and using the worksheet

Each question gives a reference amount and a difference, then asks for the compared person’s total. The set includes both larger and smaller collections, with numbers within twenty. Finding the difference between two given totals or finding an unknown reference amount are separate skills.
